speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: asked the Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (a) how frequently does the Ministry review the courses offered by the polytechnics so as to stay relevant to the needs of industries; (b) what are the two least popular courses; and (c) how many courses have been cancelled last year because of a lack of student interest.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills))
text: Popularity of a course can be measured in different ways, such as ratio of applications to places, or the aggregate score of the last student posted to the course.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills))
text: The popularity of courses changes from year to year, so I would rather not disclose which are the two least popular ones this year.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills))
text: It is also a disservice to students currently in these courses.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills))
text: Minister Ong Ye Kung will address this issue further at the upcoming Committee of Supply debates.
